# Support

Thanks for using this template. This page explains where to ask, so your
question reaches the right place and gets answered as quickly as possible.

> Looking to report a security vulnerability? Do **not** open an issue or a
> discussion. Follow the process in [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) instead.

## 1. Start with the documentation

The [documentation site](https://mauricioromagnollo.github.io/template-nextjs/)
is the fastest answer for almost every question. It covers:

- Getting started and project structure
- Styling with Tailwind CSS
- Unit testing with Vitest and the 100% coverage requirement
- End-to-end testing with Playwright
- Running the project with Docker
- Deploying to Vercel and configuring CI

Also worth a look before asking:

- The [`README.md`](../README.md) for a quick tour of the stack
- [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md) if you want to change the template itself
- Existing [issues](https://github.com/mauricioromagnollo/template-nextjs/issues?q=is%3Aissue)
  and [discussions](https://github.com/mauricioromagnollo/template-nextjs/discussions) —
  search closed ones too, since most questions have been asked before

## 2. Ask in Discussions

[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/mauricioromagnollo/template-nextjs/discussions)
is the right place for anything open-ended:

- "How would I do X with this template?"
- "Is this the intended way to structure Y?"
- Ideas you want to sanity-check before opening a feature request
- Showing off what you built from the template

Questions about Next.js, React or Tailwind in general are better asked in their
own communities — this project's Discussions are about the template itself.

## 3. Open an issue

Open an [issue](https://github.com/mauricioromagnollo/template-nextjs/issues/new/choose)
when you have something concrete and actionable:

| Situation                                               | Template        |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| Something is broken or behaves unexpectedly             | Bug report      |
| You want the template to do something it does not       | Feature request |
| The docs are missing or unclear about how to do a thing | Question        |

Issues are far easier to act on when they include a minimal reproduction: a
repository created from the template, with the smallest set of changes that
triggers the problem, plus the exact commands you ran.

## What to expect

This is a personal open source project maintained in spare time, offered under
the [MIT License](../LICENSE) with no warranty and no service-level agreement.
That said, the aim is to:

- Acknowledge new issues and discussions within **a few days**
- Triage confirmed bugs and reply with a plan or a workaround within **a week**
- Review pull requests within **a week or two**, sooner for small fixes

Security reports are handled with priority — see
[SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) for the disclosure timeline.

If something has gone quiet for more than two weeks, a polite comment on the
thread is welcome and not considered nagging.

## Helping out

The quickest way to get something fixed is often to fix it yourself. Bug fixes,
documentation improvements and answers to other people's questions are all
genuinely useful contributions — see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

Everyone taking part is expected to follow the
[Code of Conduct](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
